diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consequently, $H$ is a function of $(n,q_0,p_1)$ only.
in particular found an equivalent condition for the existence of Hamiltonians for such equations

issues.failure_explanation: The one-form eta=(p_1-p_0)dv q_0-(q_1-q_0)dv p_1 satisfies dv eta = D_n omega, which is not identically zero on Z x P(R^2) (p_0,q_0,p_1,q_1 are independent coordinates there); it vanishes only on the graph of the symplectic map. Exactness of the bicomplex (Appendix, proved on the full prolongation space) therefore does not apply; one needs the Poincare lemma on the 2-dimensional graph and, to obtain H as a function of (n,q_0,p_1), the nondegeneracy condition that (q_0,p_1) are local coordinates on the graph. Without it the claim is false: the symplectic map (q,p)->(-p,q) has p_1=q_0 on its graph and admits no type-II generating function H(n,q_0,p_1) with q_1-q_0=H_{p_1}, p_1-p_0=-H_{q_0}. The 'equivalent condition' advertised in the Conclusions is thus only one direction plus a hidden hypothesis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This implies the existence (locally) of a $(p,0)$-form

Now we are going to propose a systematic method, with which one can
proceed from a multisymplectic structure to an equivalent difference
Lagrangian structure.

Khavkine \cite{Khavkine} used this observation to prove the existence of a Lagrangian $(p,0)$-form on the full jet space, whose Euler--Lagrange equations are solved by the given multisymplectic system of PDEs. (However, these equations may be weaker than the given system and so admit other solutions.)

issues.failure_explanation: The paper obtains L only on the solution submanifold with dDh eta = dv L holding there, then concludes E(L)=I(dv L)=I(dDh eta)=0 on solutions. But I^triangle involves shift operators S_{-J} and partial derivatives in all u_J, which do not preserve equality-on-solutions, and E(L) is not even defined for a form L given only on the solution set. Moreover the existence of L uses vertical exactness on the solution submanifold, whereas Theorem A.1 proves it on the full space. The paper itself notes in Section 2 that the analogous differential step requires Khavkine's nontrivial theorem and yields possibly weaker Euler-Lagrange equations; no difference analogue is proved, so 'systematic method ... equivalent difference Lagrangian structure' is unsupported and overstated (equivalence is not obtained even in the differential case).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: immediate consequence of \eqref{eq:ii}. The exactness of the
As $\mcI^{\vartriangle}$ is a projection and the difference variational bicomplex is exact, a difference version of equality \eqref{eq:ii} holds.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts ker(I^triangle)=im(dDh) as 'an immediate consequence of (eq:ii)'. But (eq:ii) is the differential identity; its difference version was justified in Section 3 only by invoking exactness of the difference bicomplex, which is what Theorem A.2 is supposed to prove, so the argument is circular. The homotopy identity (eq:hohomo), claimed for all 1<=k<=p, is false at k=p: there dDh sigma=0 so it would give sigma=dDh h^{p,l}(sigma) for every sigma in Omega^{p,l}, contradicting I^triangle dDh=0 and I^triangle(dv u^alpha wedge vol)=dv u^alpha wedge vol != 0. The correct statement needs the extra term I^triangle(sigma) for k=p, and it is exactly this identity that would establish ker I^triangle = im dDh; it is neither stated nor verified. Also no verification of (eq:hohomo) is given for k<p.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the k=p homotopy identity sigma = dDh h^{p,l}(sigma) + I^triangle(sigma) and verify it (together with (eq:hohomo) for k<p) by direct computation with the given h^{k,l}; then derive the difference (eq:ii) from it rather than from assumed exactness, and remove the circular reference in Section 3.
issues.overall_effect: Exactness of the augmented rows at the last stage (ker I^triangle = im dDh), hence the difference version of (eq:ii), (eq:dvLag) and the coordinate-free Noether law (eq:Noecl), rest on an unproved premise; Theorem thm:added-4's proof invokes the same unproved (eq:ii). The results are very plausibly true (and partially available in the cited literature), but the paper's proof does not establish them.
